title: August and the Prom
premise: Xanthe Ishikawa, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, has spent four years keeping his head down, counting the days until graduation frees him. When he finds coded directions hidden in his late grandmother's recipe box, he learns she was once a student here—and that the directions lead to records of what the school board buried decades ago: the disappearance of scholarship students who 'transferred' and never arrived anywhere. As Xanthe deciphers the trail, he's pulled into an unlikely alliance with Priya, the prom committee chair who knows too much, and discovers the final spring audition is a cover for the board's annual purge. To survive graduation himself, Xanthe must expose the truth at the prom—turning the school's most watched night into its reckoning.
about_author: Quentin Marchetti is a former boarding-school teacher who spent six years collecting the whispered histories students never wrote down. He writes young adult fiction about quiet kids who discover the past has been waiting for them.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Establishes Ashgrove Academy's glittering surface and Xanthe's invisibility strategy: perfect grades, no friends, 94 days to graduation. A scholarship audit notice reminds him how precarious his place is. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking fear.

chapters.title: The Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Xanthe sorts his grandmother's belongings at home and finds her old Ashgrove recipe box. Among cardamom cake instructions are measurements that don't cook: ratios, dates, initials. POV Xanthe. Beat: first spark of curiosity breaking through numbness.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Xanthe tests the cipher theory in the library, matching dates to school years. The last entry is dated two weeks before his grandmother's own 'transfer' in 1971—except she didn't transfer; she graduated. POV Xanthe. Beat: unease deepening into obsession.

chapters.title: Priya Chandra Has a List
chapters.summary: Priya, prom chair and board trustee's daughter, catches Xanthe photographing archive pages. Instead of reporting him, she reveals she keeps her own list of scholarship students who vanished mid-year across decades. POV Priya. Beat: wary alliance formed over shared suspicion.

chapters.title: Ninety-Four Becomes Eighty
chapters.summary: Xanthe balances decoding with classes as the audition announcement posts: every senior must perform or forfeit diploma privileges. His stage fright collides with his need to stay near the archives. POV Xanthe. Beat: pressure mounting from all sides.

chapters.title: The West Wing Basement
chapters.summary: Following the recipe box's floor-plan sketch, Xanthe and Priya find a bricked service corridor behind the auditorium. Inside: rows of labeled lockers, each holding a confiscated student file. POV alternating. Beat: dread—the rumors were real.

chapters.title: File 1971-I
chapters.summary: They open the locker marked with his grandmother's initials. Her file details a 'withdrawal by parental request' she never made, signed by a board member whose family name still endows the library. POV Xanthe. Beat: personal betrayal; the past is his.

chapters.title: Detention Is a Tool
chapters.summary: Xanthe gets deliberately caught after curfew to map staff patrol routes. Vice-Dean Okafor watches him with unsettling knowingness but assigns only light punishment. POV Xanthe. Beat: paranoia—who can be trusted?

chapters.title: Prom as Cover
chapters.summary: Priya pulls board meeting minutes and finds the 'final audition' scheduled prom night, when alumni donors attend. She realizes the audition roster matches this year's at-risk scholarship list. POV Priya. Beat: horror crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Transferred
chapters.summary: They track down Marcus Adeyemi, expelled in 2019, now working at a diner two towns over. He confirms students get 'counseled out' before scandals break—his only crime was asking about asbestos in the dorms. POV alternating. Beat: the pattern has living victims.

chapters.title: Eight Weeks Out
chapters.summary: Midpoint. Xanthe's grades slip; his scholarship mentor warns him one more infraction means expulsion. He must choose between safety and the story. POV Xanthe. Beat: the cost becomes real.

chapters.title: What Grandma Never Said
chapters.summary: A letter hidden under the recipe box's false bottom reveals grandma stayed silent to protect her younger sister still enrolled. She left the clues hoping someone would finish it. POV Xanthe. Beat: grief transmuted into inheritance.

chapters.title: Okafor's Office
chapters.summary: Okafor summons Xanthe, shows him he knows about the basement visit—and slides back his detention slip unsigned. 'I was class of '98,' he says. 'Ask me again when you're ready.' POV Xanthe. Beat: ambiguous ally introduced.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Forced audition prep pairs Xanthe with Priya for a duet neither wanted. Between run-throughs they plan evidence copying. Their banter softens. POV Priya. Beat: love beginning against duty.

chapters.title: The Board Retreat
chapters.summary: Priya attends the trustees' winter retreat as her father's plus-one and photographs a document titled 'Senior Attrition Protocol.' Her father catches her; their fight is brutal. POV Priya. Beat: loyalty to family fractures against conscience.

chapters.title: Locker 44
chapters.summary: A current sophomore on the attrition list, Dev, goes missing after a disciplinary hearing. His locker holds a half-finished letter to his mother. POV Xanthe. Beat: urgency replaces caution—this is happening now.

chapters.title: Copy Room Confessions
chapters.summary: The pair photocopies files overnight with help from work-study student Lena, who reveals staff have whispered about 'the March list' for years. POV alternating. Beat: the conspiracy is an open secret no one dared name.

chapters.title: Six Weeks Out
chapters.summary: Xanthe receives a forged plagiarism accusation—clearly retaliation. Okafor quietly destroys it but warns: 'Next time I won't be in the room.' POV Xanthe. Beat: protected, but running out of shields.

chapters.title: Priya's Choice
chapters.summary: Her father offers Priya early admission to any university she wants if she distances herself from Ishikawa. She says yes to his face and no in her heart. POV Priya. Beat: duty and love pull apart.

chapters.title: The Archive Vault
chapters.summary: The recipe box's final clue—a key taped inside the lid—opens a deposit vault at the town bank. Grandma rented it in 1972. Inside: microfilm of board minutes naming every purge since 1954. POV Xanthe. Beat: they have the whole truth.

chapters.title: Five Weeks Out
chapters.summary: They need a way to publish without being silenced first. Lena suggests the student paper's faculty advisor, Ms. Reyes, who once sued the district. POV Priya. Beat: hope needs a vessel.

chapters.title: Ms. Reyes Reads Everything
chapters.summary: Reyes verifies the documents overnight and agrees—but insists on legal review, meaning publication lands prom week, not before. The deadline becomes the audition itself. POV alternating. Beat: the clock tightens around them.

chapters.title: Dev Comes Back
chapters.summary: Dev reappears, enrolled at a 'partner school' that doesn't exist online. His testimony completes the pattern: counseled out, relocated, erased. POV Xanthe. Beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Almost
chapters.summary: A near-kiss interrupted by patrol lights during a rooftop planning session. They laugh until it hurts. POV Priya. Beat: tenderness stolen from danger.

chapters.title: The Leak
chapters.summary: Someone reports the vault visit. Bank records show a subpoena request from the board's attorney. Whoever moves first wins. POV Xanthe. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Four Weeks Out
chapters.summary: Okafor finally tells his story: class of '98, his best friend purged, his silence bought with a job. He gives them the master key to the auditorium's sound booth. POV Okafor interlude. Beat: the adult world offering amends.

chapters.title: Prom Committee Politics
chapters.summary: Priya weaponizes her position: she schedules the senior showcase so the audition happens live on the prom stream, uncut, before donors. Her father signs off unknowingly. POV Priya. Beat: turning the enemy's stage into theirs.

chapters.title: Three Weeks Out
chapters.summary: Reyes's lawyer flags risk: publishing could void Xanthe's scholarship retroactively. He signs anyway. POV Xanthe. Beat: sacrifice chosen freely.

chapters.title: The Dress Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Full run-through of prom night logistics while hiding drives in the lighting rig. Small sabotage discovered—someone cut the booth's power line. There's a mole. POV alternating. Beat: trust tested.

chapters.title: Lena
chapters.summary: Confrontation reveals Lena tipped off Okafor months ago—not the board. But her copy-room access log leaked through a second source. Suspicion circles back to someone close. POV Xanthe. Beat: betrayal's shape unclear.

chapters.title: Two Weeks Out
chapters.summary: Priya's father disinvites her from the family's donor table; she takes it as freedom. Xanthe and Priya admit what they are to each other, quietly, between server racks. POV Priya. Beat: love declared against duty.

chapters.title: The Microfilm Backup
chapters.summary: Fearing seizure, they split the evidence: copies to Reyes, to Okafor, and mailed to a journalist. Redundancy as armor. POV Xanthe. Beat: preparation meets paranoia.

chapters.title: One Week Out
chapters.summary: The board moves the audition to a closed session—Priya's schedule gambit countered. But the prom stream contract, she realizes, can't be altered without donor consent. The loophole holds. POV Priya. Beat: checkmate pending.

chapters.title: Grandma's Song
chapters.summary: Xanthe chooses his audition piece: a song grandma wrote, lyrics doubling as the cipher key, so the audience hears the code whether or not the exposé runs. POV Xanthe. Beat: grief turned into weapon and gift.

chapters.title: Prom Night: Doors Open
chapters.summary: Gowns, string lights, donors in black ties. Xanthe in a borrowed suit, Priya running the floor, Okafor in the booth. Every glance feels like surveillance. POV alternating. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Prom Night: The Audition
chapters.summary: Xanthe performs grandma's song; the stream carries every note. Mid-song, the board cuts power—but Okafor's backup generator holds, and the audience hears the decoded names read aloud by fifty students standing one by one. POV Xanthe. Beat: climax—truth sung in public.

chapters.title: Prom Night: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Donors withdraw pledges in real time; the journalist's article publishes within the hour. Priya's father resigns on the ballroom floor. The board's attorney arrives to find cameras already rolling. POV Priya. Beat: reckoning witnessed.

chapters.title: The Days After
chapters.summary: State investigators arrive; Dev and Marcus give testimony; the west wing lockers become evidence. Xanthe's scholarship is not revoked—it endowed anew under reform terms. POV Xanthe. Beat: exhale.

chapters.title: Graduation
chapters.summary: Xanthe crosses the stage with 93 other seniors, none missing. Okafor hands him grandma's posthumous diploma, finally issued. Priya and Xanthe hold hands behind the robed rows. POV alternating. Beat: belonging earned.

chapters.title: August
chapters.summary: Epilogue. Late summer: Xanthe bakes grandma's cardamom cake in his tiny kitchen, recipe box open to a new card in his own handwriting—directions for whoever comes next. POV Xanthe. Beat: memory kept alive, love carried forward.
